long_biography.plain_text:
An assembly line was Chênevert’s first management laboratory. Fresh from production-management studies, he joined General Motors as a frontline supervisor and spent more than thirteen years advancing to responsibility for the Sainte-Thérèse plant. That practical grounding carried into aircraft-engine operations, where manufacturing leadership ultimately opened the route to corporate command.

Retirement shifted his attention from industrial scale to institutions. Through a family foundation, he has funded management education, experimental brain-tumour work and advanced cellular and gene therapy. His continuing service joins those interests: one council advises a major cancer centre, while an international board helps a Montréal business school strengthen its global network.
